MUQATIL:10:101-103/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:10:101-103/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:10:101-103/r4.claim: God saves messengers and believers from the Fire in the hereafter and grants them victory in worldly life.

TAB-FULL:v12p302/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p302/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p302/r1.claim: The people are told to await the fate of earlier nations: when punishment comes, God destroys the deniers and saves Muhammad and those who believe and follow him, as He saved earlier messengers and their believers.

TAB-FULL:v12p302/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p302/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p302/r2.claim: God's saving believers is a sure promise incumbent upon Him, as He did with earlier messengers.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1991#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1991#3/r1.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1991#3/r1.claim: Al-Rabi says God assures His audience that He saves His messengers and the believers when such punishment comes.

NAHHAS:v2p269/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p269/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p269/r3.claim: The phrase is nominative; ما is accusative after يعني and a complete noun.

SULAMI:v1p310/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p310/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p310/r1.claim: God rescues messengers from the ego's aims, heedlessness, overpowering desire, and scattered inwardness; believers are rewarded on the messengers' paths, and sincere servants are rescued.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p331/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p331/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p331/r1.claim: The verse reports God's practice with earlier nations: He saved the messengers and those who believed with them from what He inflicted on unbelievers.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p332/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p332/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p332/r1.claim: 'Likewise' means God will save believers with Muhammad from His punishment, in a deliverance like that granted to earlier believers.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p332/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p332/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p332/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas and others say 'a duty upon Us' means God has declared this promise and does not break it; what He promises must come to pass.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:10:103-108/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:10:103-108/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:10:103-108/r1.claim: In past communities, God rescued messengers and their believing followers from the punishment inflicted on unbelievers.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:10:103-108/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:10:103-108/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:10:103-108/r2.claim: Likewise, God will rescue believers through Muhammad from his punishment.

JISHUMI:v5p3437/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3437/r2.speaker: الكسائي ويعقوب
JISHUMI:v5p3437/r2.claim: Al-Kisāʾī, in one transmission, and Yaʿqūb read ننجي رسلنا lightly; the others double the jīm, two valid forms of the verb.

JISHUMI:v5p3437/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3437/r3.speaker: الكسائي ويعقوب وحفص
JISHUMI:v5p3437/r3.claim: They read كذلك حقا علينا ننج lightly; the other readers double the jīm.

JISHUMI:v5p3437/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3437/r6.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v5p3437/r6.claim: The comparison in كذلك likens the rescue of the present believers to the rescue of earlier people, and either verb may govern the phrase; حقا can be circumstantial or a verbal noun.

JISHUMI:v5p3437/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3437/r7.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v5p3437/r7.claim: Abū Muslim takes ثم as coordination with the earlier destruction: God's practice was to destroy peoples successively and then save His messengers.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p154#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p154#2/r1.speaker: يعقوب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p154#2/r1.claim: Yaqub reads ننجي lightly, with a variant report about this reading; the believers are saved with the messengers when punishment descends.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p154#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p154#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p154#2/r2.claim: The future verb means “We saved,” while likewise denotes “as We saved them”; حقا means obligatory.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p154#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p154#2/r3.speaker: الكسائي وحفص ويعقوب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p154#2/r3.claim: Al-Kisai, Hafs, and Yaqub read ننج with a light form; the other readers read it doubled, and نجا and أنجى have the same meaning.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p354#4/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p354#4/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p354#4/r2.claim: ‘Then We save’ coordinates with an omitted statement: God destroys nations, then saves messengers, recounting past events.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p354#4/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p354#4/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p354#4/r3.claim: The believers saved are those who believed with the messengers; similarly God will rescue believers and destroy polytheists.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p354#4/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p354#4/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p354#4/r4.claim: ‘An obligation upon Us’ is parenthetical emphasis that this rescue is truly binding upon God.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p354#4/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p354#4/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p354#4/r5.claim: A reading has ننج with a doubled jīm.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p145#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p145#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p145#2/r2.claim: Because the punishment's duration is unspecified while the Prophet and believers remain among disbelievers, God explicitly states that His established practice is to rescue messengers and their followers, making the threat more severe.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p145#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p145#2/r3.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p145#2/r3.claim: All but al-Kisa'i and Hafs read ننجي with a doubled jīm; they read it with a quiescent first nūn and a light jīm. Other reported forms are called baseless by al-Zajjaj, and the written form omits yāʾ after jīm.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p145#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p145#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p145#2/r4.claim: كذلك can be nominative or accusative as an adjective describing an omitted verbal noun.

TABRISI:10:103#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:10:103#2/r10.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:10:103#2/r10.claim: Hasan says that as God rescued earlier prophets and their followers when destroying their communities, He will rescue Muhammad and those who believe in him.

TABRISI:10:103#2/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:10:103#2/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:10:103#2/r11.claim: Another interpretation calls rescue an obligation upon God through wisdom and takes it as saving believers from the hereafter's punishment, just as from worldly punishment.

TABRISI:10:103#2/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:10:103#2/r12.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABRISI:10:103#2/r12.claim: Al-Sadiq urges his companions to testify that those among them who die holding this commitment belong to Paradise, invoking God's promise to rescue believers.

TABRISI:10:103#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:10:103#2/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:10:103#2/r8.claim: God saves the messengers and believers from punishment when it falls.

TABRISI:10:103#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:10:103#2/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:10:103#2/r9.claim: An alternative says He saves believers from the harms and plots of their enemies.

TABRISI:10:103/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:10:103/r1.speaker: الكسائي، يعقوب
TABRISI:10:103/r1.claim: Al-Kisa'i through Nasir and Yaqub through Rawh read ثم ننجي رسلنا lightly; Rawh is also reported to have the doubled reading, while the others read it doubled.

TABRISI:10:103/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:10:103/r10.speaker: جامع العلوم النحوي الضرير
TABRISI:10:103/r10.claim: The grammarian says حقا may instead be appositional to كذلك or an adjective, but one verb cannot govern both كذلك and حقا as two verbal nouns or two states.

TABRISI:10:103/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:10:103/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:10:103/r11.claim: If كذلك modifies the first ننجي and حقا modifies the second, the pause should come after كذلك.

TABRISI:10:103/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:10:103/r2.speaker: الكسائي، حفص عن عاصم، يعقوب، سهل
TABRISI:10:103/r2.claim: Al-Kisa'i, Hafs from Asim, Yaqub, and Sahl read ننجي المؤمنين lightly; the others double it.

TABRISI:10:103/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:10:103/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:10:103/r3.claim: The light reading is supported by the Qur'anic verb أنجاه in the account of Abraham being saved from the fire.

TABRISI:10:103/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:10:103/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:10:103/r4.claim: The doubled reading is supported by the Qur'anic form ونجينا; both readings are sound.

TABRISI:10:103/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:10:103/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:10:103/r5.claim: The cited poetic line likewise uses نجى for saving a person from danger.

TABRISI:10:103/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:10:103/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:10:103/r6.claim: Looking is seeking a thing through thought as sight seeks perception; nذر is the plural of a warner, and waiting means remaining in place for what is expected.

TABRISI:10:103/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:10:103/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:10:103/r7.claim: A mithl within one genus substitutes for its counterpart in its essential nature, while a cross-genus likeness is proximity by analogy; salvation and safety both derive from rising above harm or receiving something unharmed.

TABRISI:10:103/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:10:103/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:10:103/r8.claim: The phrase كذلك may describe believers' rescue as resembling the rescue of earlier believers, a right due upon God; grammatically it may be governed by either instance of ننجي.

TABRISI:10:103/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:10:103/r9.speaker: أبو مسلم
TABRISI:10:103/r9.claim: Abu Muslim takes حقا as a circumstantial accusative although its form resembles a verbal noun.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p69/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p69/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p69/r1.claim: When punishment falls, God saves the messengers and their believers; no people were destroyed without their prophet and believers being rescued.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p69/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p69/r2.speaker: يعقوب وحفص والكسائي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p69/r2.claim: These readers, including the stated transmission from Abu Bakr, read nunajj al-mu'minin with a light form.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p69/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p69/r3.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p69/r3.claim: One interpretation is saving believers from punishment when it comes upon the deniers.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p69/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p69/r4.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p69/r4.claim: Another interpretation is saving believers from Hell in the afterlife.

QURTUBI-FULL:10:103/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:103/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:10:103/r1.claim: When God sends punishment on a people, His practice is to remove the messengers and believers from among them and save them.

QURTUBI-FULL:10:103/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:103/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:10:103/r2.claim: ‘A duty upon Us’ means God’s promise must be fulfilled because He has stated it and never breaks His word.

QURTUBI-FULL:10:103/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:103/r3.speaker: يعقوب
QURTUBI-FULL:10:103/r3.claim: Ya‘qub reads the verb for saving the messengers in a light form.

QURTUBI-FULL:10:103/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:103/r4.speaker: الكسائي وحفص ويعقوب
QURTUBI-FULL:10:103/r4.claim: Al-Kisa’i, Hafs, and Ya‘qub read the verb ‘save the believers’ in a light form, while the other readers use the doubled form; both are eloquent forms with the same meaning.

BAYDAWI-FULL:10:101-103/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:101-103/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:101-103/r4.claim: The promise to rescue messengers and believers is coordinated with an omitted statement that earlier peoples are destroyed, and may apply to Muhammad and his companions when the polytheists are destroyed.

BAYDAWI-FULL:10:101-103/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:101-103/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:101-103/r5.claim: God's rescue of believers is an assured duty by His promise; Hafs and al-Kisa'i read nunajji in the shortened form.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p143#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p143#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p143#5/r1.claim: The clause continues the account: God destroys nations and then saves His messengers and those who believed with them.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p143#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p143#5/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p143#5/r2.claim: God rescues believers among the addressed people in the same way He rescued earlier believers, while destroying the polytheists; حقا علينا is a parenthetical emphatic statement.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p143#5/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p143#5/r3.speaker: علي وحفص
NASAFI-FULL:v2p143#5/r3.claim: They read nunajji with the light form.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p110/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p110/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p110/r1.claim: After recalling the destruction of earlier nations that denied messengers, God recounts how He then rescued the messengers and believers, promising the same rescue to Muhammad's believers.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p110/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p110/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p110/r2.claim: He connects the verse to an omitted statement, understood as: We destroy the nations, then rescue Our messengers, as in prior accounts.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p110/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p110/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p110/r3.claim: ظاهرًا, كذلك is an adverb meaning God rescues those who believe in Muhammad as He rescued earlier messengers and their believers; حقا means that promise is truly binding.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p110/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p110/r4.speaker: أبو البقاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p110/r4.claim: He permits حقا as a substitute for the omitted noun implied by the comparison, and offers alternatives in which كذلك and حقا are governed by one or the other occurrence of ننجي.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p110/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p110/r5.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p110/r5.claim: He allows the comparison particle to be nominative in an implied sentence, الأمر كذلك, with حقا governed by the following verb.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p110/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p110/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p110/r6.claim: He glosses it as rescuing believers and destroying disbelievers in the same way, with حقا علينا as an inserted assertion.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p110/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p110/r7.speaker: القاضي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p110/r7.claim: He takes حقا علينا as an obligation: rescuing messengers and believers into reward is required, otherwise imposing hard duties would not be fitting.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p110/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p110/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p110/r8.claim: The response is that God's right is established by His promise and judgment, not by creatures deserving anything from their Creator.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p110/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p110/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p110/r9.claim: Al-Kisa'i and Hafs read ننجي with lightening from أنجى; the written consonantal form omits the yāʾ.

SAMIN-DURR:10:103/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:103/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:10:103/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari connects ثم ننجي to an omitted discourse inferred from the preceding clause: God destroys past peoples, then saves His messengers.

SAMIN-DURR:10:103/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:103/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:10:103/r2.claim: كذلك is most likely an accusative phrase meaning that God saves believers in the same manner as He saved earlier messengers and their believers.

SAMIN-DURR:10:103/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:103/r3.speaker: ابن عطية وأبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:10:103/r3.claim: They allow كذلك to be the predicate of an omitted subject: الأمر كذلك.

SAMIN-DURR:10:103/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:103/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:10:103/r4.claim: حقا may be governed by an omitted verb, apposed to the omitted noun represented by كذلك, governed with كذلك by ننجي, or governed separately by the two forms of ننجي.

SAMIN-DURR:10:103/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:103/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:10:103/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reads the saving as believers being delivered from the disbelievers, who are destroyed; حقا علينا is parenthetical.

SAMIN-DURR:10:103/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:103/r6.speaker: الكسائي وحفص
SAMIN-DURR:10:103/r6.claim: Al-Kisa'i and Hafs read ننجي المؤمنين with a light form from أنجى; the common difference is reported here, while Abu Ali al-Ahwazi also records it in 10:92 and the earlier clause.

SAMIN-DURR:10:103/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:103/r7.speaker: أبو علي الأهوازي
SAMIN-DURR:10:103/r7.claim: Abu Ali al-Ahwazi reports the reading difference also in فاليوم ننجيك ببدنك and ثم ننجي رسلنا; the Qur'anic codices write ننج without a yāʾ.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p299#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p299#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p299#2/r2.claim: The deniers await punishment like earlier nations; God destroys the deniers and saves His messengers and believers, a deliverance He has made binding upon Himself.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p299#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p299#2/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p299#2/r3.claim: A hadith in both Sahih collections says God wrote that His mercy precedes His anger.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p492/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p492/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p492/r1.claim: God's pattern in earlier nations was to punish those who rejected messengers and then save believers, just as He will save Muhammad and his followers.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p492/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p492/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p492/r2.claim: The present-tense rescue re-enacts past events as a warning; ثم signals the prolonged trial and elevated rank of rescue, while omission of the opposite clause keeps focus on glad tidings.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p492/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p492/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p492/r3.claim: The saved include everyone who truly believed with the messengers, even those at the lowest rank, encouraging others to emulate them.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p492/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p492/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p492/r4.claim: God's obligation to save believers applies in every age, even without a living messenger among them; alternatively, the author parses كذلك as a subject and ننج المؤمنين as its predicate.

DURR-FULL:v4p393/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p393/r7.speaker: الربيع
DURR-FULL:v4p393/r7.claim: God first warns of torment and vengeance, then promises to save His messengers and believers when punishment comes.

BURSEVI:v4p48#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p48#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p48#2/r1.claim: The verse connects to an implied preceding clause: God destroys past peoples, then saves messengers and believers as if narrating those past events in the present.

BURSEVI:v4p48#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p48#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p48#2/r2.claim: ‘Just so’ describes deliverance; ‘truly upon Us’ interrupts the verb and object, with an understood verb meaning the promise is truly established.

BURSEVI:v4p48#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p48#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p48#2/r3.claim: God's established practice is to save believers from every hardship and punishment, as He saved earlier messengers and followers and fulfilled His promise; this continues while the law and its practice remain.

BURSEVI:v4p48#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p48#2/r4.speaker: السعدي
BURSEVI:v4p48#2/r4.claim: Saʿdī's couplet says a beloved who loves you will not leave you in an enemy's hands.

BURSEVI:v4p48#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p48#2/r5.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v4p48#2/r5.claim: The Prophet calls death a believer's gift: the righteous rest from worldly toil in barzakh, while the wicked relieve others of harm and enter spiritual punishment.

BURSEVI:v4p48#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p48#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p48#2/r6.claim: The best worship is waiting for relief because it brings ease of heart and patience's reward; trusting that God alone removes affliction reduces pain and panic.

BURSEVI:v4p48#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p48#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p48#2/r7.claim: An ignorant sufferer may forget divine decree and gentleness, think relief impossible, implicitly attribute impotence to God, and remain distressed.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p196/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p196/r1.speaker: الكسائي ويعقوب
ALUSI-FULL:v11p196/r1.claim: Al-Kisāʾī and Yaʿqūb read ننجي with a light jīm; the standard reading doubles it.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p196/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p196/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p196/r2.claim: The rescue clause follows an implied statement that earlier nations were destroyed; the intervening text hastens the threat, and this passage narrates destruction before rescue.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p196/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p196/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p196/r3.claim: The present-tense rescue vividly recounts a past event; believers are saved as in prior instances, and the concluding sentence reaffirms this outcome.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p196/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p196/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p196/r4.claim: That rescue is a sure divine promise, termed obligatory only figuratively, since nothing truly imposes an obligation on God.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p196/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p196/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p196/r5.claim: Believers may mean all believers, including messengers and followers, or only followers; messengers are omitted in the latter reading because they were already named.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p196/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p196/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p196/r6.claim: The concluding clause teaches that faith is the basis of rescue and seals the preceding statement by reaffirming its meaning.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p298/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p298/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p298/r3.claim: The promise to save the messengers follows the threatened days: God reassures the Prophet and believers that He will save them as He saved earlier messengers.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p298/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p298/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p298/r4.claim: “Thus” is a concluding summary referring back to the deliverance just promised.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p298/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p298/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p298/r5.claim: “A duty upon Us” is parenthetical and treats deliverance as a graciously honored commitment from God.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p298/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p298/r6.speaker: الكسائي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p298/r6.claim: Al-Kisa'i reads the second nun quiescent and the jīm light, from the form inja; the meaning matches the other reading.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p298/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p298/r7.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p298/r7.claim: Hafs from Asim shares al-Kisa'i's light-jīm reading; other readers use a doubled jīm, with the same meaning.

TABATABAI:10:100-103/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:10:100-103/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:10:100-103/r6.claim: “Then We save Our messengers and those who believed” completes the threat about earlier peoples; “wait” interrupts it as a reply directed to the deniers.

TABATABAI:10:100-103/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:10:100-103/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:10:100-103/r7.claim: The interruption suits the warning because the Prophet awaits the judgment with them, while he and the believers—not the Prophet alone—await deliverance from punishment.

TABATABAI:10:103/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:10:103/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:10:103/r1.claim: As God saved earlier messengers and their believers when punishment came, He promises to save the believers of this community; “as a true obligation upon Us” is an absolute-object construction and “the believers” refers to this community.

TABATABAI:10:103/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:10:103/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:10:103/r2.claim: The verse may subtly suggest that the Prophet will not live to see the judgment, since only this community’s believers are named; the author presents this as a possible inference, supported by repeated statements about dying before the return.

ASAD-NOTES:10:103#n125/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:10:103#n125/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:10:103#n125/r1.claim: Thumma connects to the recurring history of earlier prophets, their communities' rejection and doom, and God's deliverance of prophets and followers, rather than the immediately preceding passage.

ASAD-NOTES:10:103#n125/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:10:103#n125/r2.speaker: Rashid Rida'
ASAD-NOTES:10:103#n125/r2.claim: Rashid Rida' calls this an outstanding example of the Qur'an's concise, elliptical expression; Asad agrees with that assessment.

ASAD-NOTES:10:103#n126/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:10:103#n126/r1.speaker: Razi
ASAD-NOTES:10:103#n126/r1.claim: Razi reads God's self-imposed promise as logical necessity and fulfillment of His will, not an obligation or duty imposed on God by anyone.

ASAD-NOTES:10:99#n124/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:10:99#n124/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:10:99#n124/r1.claim: Unbelief results from an a priori refusal to use reason to understand God's revealed messages and the evidence in creation.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: When a nation faces God’s law it no longer accepts faith; Jonah’s people were the exception, and believers should use intellect rather than wait for coercive punishment signs.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Prophet is told to wait for the decisive punishment just as his deniers wait for it.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: People should reflect on signs in the inner and outer world; those demanding punishment should wait, as the Prophet does, while God delivers messengers and believers.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Decisive punishment destroys all except God’s messengers and their believers; this warns Quraysh that God will seize them and protect believers according to His established practice.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: This protection rule concerns punishment of messenger-rejecting nations; ordinary reminder trials affect believers and disbelievers alike, though believers benefit and disbelievers lose their excuse.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:10:99/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:10:99/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:10:99/r1.claim: These verses affirm God’s control of the universe and supreme power, encourage the Prophet not to lose heart before persistent unbelievers, and warn that forcing faith wrongly puts human will above God’s.

QIRAAT-ER:10:103:11#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:10:103:11#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:10:103:11#1/r1.claim: Form II indicates intensive repeated rescue rather than Form IV's single act and mirrors the standard reading at word 2.

QIRAAT-ER:10:103:11#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:10:103:11#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:10:103:11#2/r1.claim: Retaining final yāʾ avoids apocopation and makes the imperfect indicative rather than jussive.

QIRAAT-ER:10:103:2#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:10:103:2#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:10:103:2#1/r1.claim: Form IV suggests a single decisive rescue rather than intensive repeated deliverance, aligning with the second nunjī.

QIRAAT-ER:10:103:3#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:10:103:3#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:10:103:3#1/r1.claim: Sukūn on sīn is a lighter dialectal form with the same meaning.

STUDYQURAN:10:103/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:10:103/r1.speaker: Bg, IK, JJ, Kl, Ṭ, Z
STUDYQURAN:10:103/r1.claim: Although “save” is present tense, it refers to earlier messengers and means God saved them.

STUDYQURAN:10:103/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:10:103/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:10:103/r2.claim: God will deliver Muhammad and his followers from Makkan persecution, as He delivered earlier messengers and their followers from persecutors.

STUDYQURAN:10:intro/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:10:intro/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:10:intro/r10.claim: Believers receive glad tidings and are urged to remain patient through hardships inflicted by disbelievers.
